llm.summary: This is a documentation-only iOS development skill with disclosed local memory use and no evidence of hidden execution, exfiltration, or credential storage.

dimensions.detail: The macOS/Xcode requirement and use of xcodebuild, simctl, devicectl, codesign, plutil, and related tools are proportionate for native iOS development.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts are markdown/json only, with no executable install scripts or automatic package/plugin mutation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are specific to iOS work and referenced guide files; destructive actions are called out as requiring explicit confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally reads and writes local Clawic memory under ~/Clawic/data, including iOS project records and limited shared device/contact/project/subscription records; this is disclosed, scoped to durable development context, and paired with rules forbidding secret storage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities match its stated iOS platform-development purpose: guidance for lifecycle, permissions, entitlements, releases, crashes, StoreKit, privacy, and related Xcode tooling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install if you want persistent iOS project memory across sessions. Review the ~/Clawic/data paths first if you do not want device identifiers, client/project names, release history, or Apple Developer Program renewal details stored locally; do not store actual passwords, private keys, API key bodies, or demo-account passwords there.
llm.findings: [RA2] expected: The persistence behavior is real, but it is explicitly documented as local project memory for iOS work, includes destination rules and secret-stripping requirements, and shows no network transmission or hidden collection. Users should still be aware it may retain app, device, client, project, and subscription metadata across sessions.
